title: Application Security Engineer
tagline: Help developers build software that is secure by design.
about: Application security engineers work alongside development teams so that security is built in from the start: reviewing designs, setting up automated checks in CI, writing secure-coding guidance and helping teams fix issues quickly.
It suits developers who enjoy security, since the job is as much about enabling other engineers as it is about finding problems.
day: Run threat-modelling sessions on new features
Review code and designs for security issues
Maintain automated security checks in CI
Triage reported issues and guide fixes

phases.title: Programming foundations
phases.goal: Write small programs confidently and use the tools every developer uses daily.

nodes.d: Pick Python and get fluent with the basics before anything else. Fluency in one language transfers to every other.
links: CS50x: Harvard's intro to computer science

nodes.d: Developers live in the command line: navigating files, running programs and chaining tools together.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)
OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Version control is non-negotiable: every job uses it. Commit early, branch for experiments, open pull requests.
Break problems down, read errors calmly, use a debugger and print statements deliberately.
links: Exercism: practice in 70+ languages with mentoring

phases.title: Web development first
phases.goal: You can only secure software you understand how to build.

nodes.d: Build a small app with a backend, database and login so you understand what you'll be reviewing.
How login, sessions, tokens and permissions are meant to work.
CIA triad, least privilege, defence in depth and trust boundaries.

phases.title: Secure development
phases.goal: Prevent the most common classes of weakness.

nodes.d: The most common categories of web application risk and how to prevent each.
Turn guidance into checklists and requirements teams can follow.
Ask 'what could go wrong?' at design time, when fixes are cheapest.
Read code with a defender's eye and give actionable fixes.
links: CWE Top 25 Most Dangerous Software Weaknesses

project.d: Threat-model your own web app, review its code against the ASVS, fix what you find and document the decisions.

phases.title: Security at scale
phases.goal: Make secure the default across many teams.

nodes.d: Automated static analysis, dependency and secret scanning on every pull request.
Know what you ship and where it came from.
links: SLSA: supply-chain levels for software artifacts

nodes.d: Secure defaults for infrastructure your apps run on.
Champions programmes, training and metrics that improve outcomes.

project.d: Add SAST, dependency and secret scanning to a project's CI with clear triage rules, and write a one-page secure-coding guide for its contributors.

interview: Review a code snippet and explain the weakness and the fix.
Threat-model a feature on a whiteboard.
Explain how you'd roll out security tooling without slowing teams down.
Web fundamentals: auth, sessions, HTTP and common weakness classes.
